description: Estimate prior probabilities from occurrence data, habitat, and spatial modeling

functions.name: generate_domestic_food_priors
functions.description: Adds named Beta(alpha, beta) prior rows for domestic/commensal animal species, human food/crop species, and (optionally) candidate cultivated plants -- a non-GBIF prior source using live iNaturalist casual-grade evidence, for the gap where occurrence-database indexing structurally under-counts captive/cultivated organisms. Output is bind_rows()-compatible with estimate_kernel_priors()'s taxaexpect_priors

inputs.name: model_obj
inputs.description: Output of estimate_kernel_priors() (current recommended path -- pass the POOLED fit, not a sampling_group_col-grouped one, since a domestic/food species isn't scoped to one detection process); used only for N_total and habitat_col so these rows sit on the same theta scale as the rest of taxaexpect_priors

inputs.name: lat
inputs.description: Query site latitude for the iNaturalist search

inputs.name: lng
inputs.description: Query site longitude for the iNaturalist search

inputs.name: grid_id
inputs.description: Grid cell identifier attached to every output row, for joining into taxaexpect_priors

inputs.name: domestic_animal_taxa
inputs.description: Domestic/commensal animal taxon names. Default is a pre-populated starting list (dog, cat, cow, sheep, pig, chicken, horse, Homo sapiens, etc.). Set to character(0) to disable this channel

inputs.name: food_species_taxa
inputs.description: Human food/crop species taxon names, a separate contamination category from domestic_animal_taxa (food-handling/lab-bench contamination, not pet/livestock). Default is a pre-populated starting list. Set to character(0) to disable

inputs.name: candidate_plant_taxa
inputs.description: Candidate plant-kingdom taxa (e.g. from your study's own plant-kingdom BLAST/GBIF matches) to check for real local cultivated/casual-grade iNaturalist evidence. Default NULL (channel disabled, no live iNaturalist calls made unless supplied)

inputs.name: radius_km
inputs.description: iNaturalist search radius

inputs.name: taxonomy
inputs.description: Optional taxon_name + rank columns (incl. kingdom) joined onto the result. Supplying a kingdom column enables an iNaturalist cross-kingdom-homonym check

inputs.name: api_token
inputs.description: iNaturalist API token; defaults to the INAT_API_TOKEN environment variable

output.description: One row per resolved domestic/food/plant taxon: taxon_name (always populated, unlike generate_undetected_diversity()'s anonymous proxies), grid_id, alpha, beta, theta_mean, theta_sd, model_tier ('tier_domestic_food'), prior_source_type ('domestic_animal'/'food_species'/'domestic_plant'), inat_n_observations_local, inat_kingdom, inat_kingdom_mismatch

functions.scaling_note: iNaturalist API; seconds to ~1 min depending on how many candidate_plant_taxa are supplied

functions.name: calibrate_kernel_bandwidth
functions.description: Kernel-priors path (2026-08-30/31 redesign), a site-centered distance-kernel alternative to the archived GLMM/grid-cell prediction path (the whole grid/GLMM chain -- build_priors/optimize_grid_size/prepare_model_dataframe/train_biodiversity_model/generate_full_priors/etc. -- was archived 2026-09-09, see TaxaExpect/CLAUDE.md's 2026-09-09 session note). Selects the kernel bandwidth (lambda_km, and optionally a covariate bandwidth) via leave-one-block-out composition prediction -- replaces the GLMM path's AIC formula screening. Offline, no network calls, seconds.

inputs.name: occurrence_data
inputs.description: Standardized occurrence data with lat/lon/main_habitat/taxon_name columns (std_occurrences)

inputs.name: site_habitat
inputs.description: Focal habitat to restrict the calibration/estimation to (e.g. 'Marine')

inputs.name: lambda_grid
inputs.description: Candidate bandwidths (km) to try

inputs.name: covariate_col
inputs.description: Optional numeric covariate column (e.g. 'depth_m') for a second, covariate-space kernel factor

inputs.name: lambda_covariate_grid
inputs.description: Candidate covariate bandwidths, only used when covariate_col is supplied

inputs.name: block_size_deg
inputs.description: Spatial block size (degrees) for the leave-one-block-out cross-validation

inputs.name: min_block_records
inputs.description: Minimum records a block needs to be scored

output.description: $best (the chosen lambda_km/lambda_covariate + its LOBO loss), $results (loss for every grid point tried, plus 'regional'/'nearest_block' reference rows)

functions.scaling_note: Offline, no network calls; seconds for a typical real dataset

functions.name: estimate_kernel_priors
functions.description: The current recommended prior-generation path. Site-centered distance-kernel weighting (geo x optional-covariate product kernel), replacing gridding + GLMM prediction entirely -- there is no create_sites_from_grid()/model-fitting step in this path at all. Produces a priors object structurally compatible with the archived GLMM path's generate_full_priors() output (bind_rows()-compatible taxaexpect_priors), so every downstream consumer (join_priors(), generate_domestic_food_priors(), etc.) works unchanged.

inputs.name: occurrence_data
inputs.description: Standardized occurrence data with lat/lon/main_habitat/taxon_name columns (std_occurrences)

inputs.name: site_lat
inputs.description: Focal site latitude

inputs.name: site_lon
inputs.description: Focal site longitude

inputs.name: site_habitat
inputs.description: Focal habitat (e.g. 'Marine')

inputs.name: lambda_km
inputs.description: Kernel bandwidth in km -- use calibrate_kernel_bandwidth()'s $best$lambda_km rather than guessing

inputs.name: m
inputs.description: Pseudo-record count for the regional back-off prior

inputs.name: covariate_col
inputs.description: Optional numeric covariate column (e.g. 'depth_m'); must match calibrate_kernel_bandwidth()'s own covariate_col if used

inputs.name: site_covariate
inputs.description: The focal site's own covariate value (e.g. mean depth of nearby records), required when covariate_col is supplied

inputs.name: lambda_covariate
inputs.description: Covariate-space bandwidth, from calibrate_kernel_bandwidth()'s $best$lambda_covariate

inputs.name: site_id
inputs.description: Site identifier stamped onto every output row (e.g. sprintf('Site_%.2f_%.2f', site_lat, site_lon)) -- used downstream as this path's grid_id equivalent

inputs.name: sampling_group_col
inputs.description: 2026-09-03, added. Column identifying which detection PROCESS/METHOD each row belongs to (e.g. 'fish' vs 'birds' vs 'phytoplankton' surveyed with different effort) -- NOT the same thing as a physical site. Optional but NOT safe to omit: with no sampling_group_col, every record is pooled regardless of detection process, with no warning or error, even when that means silently mixing genuinely incompatible processes. When supplied, theta AND the Good-Turing budget (f1/f2/missing_mass/chao_missing/theta_present) are computed WITHIN each group rather than pooled, since both are shared-denominator quantities a barely-sampled group's singletons would otherwise dilute. With more than one group the pooled f1/f2/chao_missing/theta_present scalars are NA by design and $budget is authoritative. No-op for a taxonomically homogeneous pool. Build this column yourself BY HAND (e.g. a case_when() over taxonomic rank columns), from real knowledge of detection methodology -- there is no automated way to detect a comparable detection method from taxonomy or data alone, and this function does not require pre-merged, sample-size-adequate groups (it produces honestly wide uncertainty for a sparse group on its own), so classify at whatever granularity genuinely reflects distinct detection methods

output.description: $priors (the taxaexpect_priors-shaped data frame: taxon_name, alpha, beta, theta_mean, theta_sd, prior_branch='resident_observed', effective_records), $params (incl. site_id), $n_eff, $missing_mass, $budget (per-group budget table when sampling_group_col supplied) -- pass the WHOLE object (not just $priors) to generate_undetected_diversity()/generate_domestic_food_priors() as model_obj

functions.scaling_note: Offline, no network calls; seconds for a typical real dataset

functions.name: generate_undetected_diversity
functions.description: Unseen-taxa floor (Good-Turing/Chao-based dark-diversity mirrors) for the kernel-priors path, the kernel analog of what the archived GLMM path's generate_full_priors() used to compute internally. Output is bind_rows()-compatible with estimate_kernel_priors()'s own $priors.

inputs.name: model_obj
inputs.description: Output of estimate_kernel_priors() (the whole object, not just $priors)

inputs.name: jeffreys_threshold
inputs.description: Minimum singleton count before falling back to a Jeffreys-bounds floor

inputs.name: singleton_ess
inputs.description: Effective sample size assigned to each singleton mirror row

inputs.name: taxonomy
inputs.description: Occurrence data (e.g. the same std_occurrences fed to estimate_kernel_priors()) used to derive higher-rank taxonomy for the dark-diversity mirrors

output.description: Anonymous dark-diversity/undetected prior rows, prior_branch='resident_undetected', bind_rows()-compatible with estimate_kernel_priors()'s $priors

functions.name: apply_undetected_evidence
functions.description: 2026-09-07, new -- advanced/optional: elevates the dark-diversity floor for specific NAMED unobserved taxa using outside evidence (regional GBIF proximity just outside the study bbox, invasive/nonindigenous watch-list status, or iNaturalist range checks -- each its own evidence generator, e.g. generate_regional_proximity_evidence()/generate_invasive_watch_evidence()/generate_inat_range_evidence(), not covered by this entry). Metadata-only (no graph edge) -- this needs a real evidence table as input, which itself needs case-by-case design (a watch list, a regional-proximity search radius, etc.) rather than a one-size default; wire in directly if you have a specific evidence source, following the real production kernel-priors workflows' own pattern.

inputs.name: taxaexpect_priors
inputs.description: The priors table so far (e.g. estimate_kernel_priors()'s $priors + generate_undetected_diversity()'s output, already bind_rows()'d)

inputs.name: model_obj
inputs.description: Output of estimate_kernel_priors()

inputs.name: evidence
inputs.description: taxon_name + weight (+ p_conc) rows from an evidence generator -- see description

inputs.name: grid_id
inputs.description: Site id to elevate priors at (e.g. model_obj$params$site_id)

inputs.name: main_habitat
inputs.description: Habitat to stamp on elevated rows

inputs.name: taxonomy
inputs.description: Occurrence data for deriving elevated rows' higher-rank taxonomy

inputs.name: pricing
inputs.description: 'blend' (linear weight*ceiling) or 'curve' (per-sampling-group Good-Turing budget pricing)

output.description: Elevated prior rows for the named evidence taxa, bind_rows()-compatible with the rest of taxaexpect_priors

functions.scaling_note: Offline once the evidence table exists; the evidence generators themselves may make live GBIF/iNaturalist calls

functions.name: plot_theta_surface
functions.description: The kernel-priors path's own visualizer (2026-09-01): a static (default) or optionally interactive KDE prior-field map for ONE taxon, evaluating estimate_kernel_priors()'s same estimator on a full grid via binned FFT convolution instead of at one site. Replaces the archived plot_theta_map_interactive() (which parsed Grid_<lat>_<lon> ids into centroids -- archived 2026-09-09 along with the rest of the GLMM chain, since it had nothing to draw for a single opaque kernel site_id) -- this is now the package's only prior-field visualization. Genuinely scriptable (interactive=FALSE is the default, a real static plot, not a Shiny gadget with no non-interactive path) -- unlike review_spatial_flags()/review_institution_flags()/review_spatial_context(), which have no non-interactive mode at all and so have no graph representation by design.

inputs.name: kernel_fit
inputs.description: Output of estimate_kernel_priors() (the whole object)

inputs.name: occurrence_data
inputs.description: The same standardized occurrence data fed to estimate_kernel_priors()

inputs.name: taxon
inputs.description: Which taxon_name to render the prior field for (one taxon per call)

inputs.name: n_grid
inputs.description: Grid resolution (n_grid x n_grid lattice)

inputs.name: covariate_at
inputs.description: Fixed covariate value to evaluate the surface at, if the kernel fit used one (e.g. a depth). Omitting it on a covariate-fit surface renders an explicitly labeled 'covariate omitted' map, never a silently wrong one

inputs.name: interactive
inputs.description: FALSE (default) renders a static base-R plot; TRUE renders an interactive leaflet map (requires leaflet)

output.description: A static plot (default) or leaflet htmlwidget (interactive=TRUE) of the prior field for the requested taxon

functions.scaling_note: ~1-2s per taxon for a 512x512 grid from ~1M occurrence records, after the shared kernel FFT is computed once per call

functions.name: condition_evidence_on_habitat
functions.description: Multiplies each evidence row's presence weight by the taxon's own weight for the site habitat, floored at the weight a taxon with no evidence at all receives -- so undetected-evidence rows (regional proximity, invasive watch, etc.) obey the residents' habitat stratification instead of bleeding evenly across habitats regardless of suitability.

inputs.name: evidence
inputs.description: Data frame with taxon_name and weight columns (any evidence generator's output, e.g. generate_regional_proximity_evidence())

inputs.name: habitat_lookup
inputs.description: Output of TaxaHabitat::build_habitat_lookup(): taxon_name plus one numeric weight column per habitat class

inputs.name: site_habitat
inputs.description: Character scalar naming the site's habitat column in habitat_lookup

inputs.name: w_floor
inputs.description: The weight below which no evidence row may fall -- pass the run's clamp weight (w_scale * exp(-d_cap/d_half) under curve pricing)

inputs.name: verbose
inputs.description: Report counts

output.description: evidence with weight replaced by the conditioned weight, plus habitat_weight (H_site, NA when unknown), weight_unconditioned (the generator's original weight), habitat_floored (TRUE where the product fell below w_floor)

functions.scaling_note: Fast; pure R computation over an already-built evidence table and habitat lookup

functions.name: generate_regional_proximity_evidence
functions.description: A thin, two-stage evidence generator for apply_undetected_evidence(): for each taxon with no in-bbox occurrence record, cheaply checks (via GBIF density tiles) whether GBIF has ANY record nearby at all before paying for a real filtered occurrence fetch, then derives a distance-decayed presence weight and an age-decayed confidence.

inputs.name: zero_bbox_taxa
inputs.description: Taxon names with no in-bbox occurrence record this run -- typically every named candidate absent from taxaexpect_priors entirely

inputs.name: lat
inputs.description: The study site's own latitude (both stages search around this point)

inputs.name: lng
inputs.description: The study site's own longitude

inputs.name: d_half
inputs.description: Distance (km) at which weight decays to half its maximum

inputs.name: w_scale
inputs.description: Near-boundary presence probability ceiling: weight = w_scale * exp(-distance_km/d_half). The default 1 is almost certainly too high for any real study -- calibrate against a local expert checklist (GreatLakes2023 adopted 0.05)

inputs.name: age_half
inputs.description: Record age (years) at which p_conc decays to half its fresh-record value of 1

inputs.name: tile_zoom
inputs.description: Forwarded to TaxaFlag::check_gbif_tile_range(zoom=) for Stage 1

inputs.name: buffer_margin
inputs.description: Stage 2's fetch radius is Stage 1's own dist_nearest_occupied_km times this margin, clamped to [min_buffer_km, max_buffer_km]

inputs.name: min_buffer_km
inputs.description: Floor on Stage 2's fetch radius regardless of what Stage 1 reported

inputs.name: max_buffer_km
inputs.description: Ceiling on Stage 2's fetch radius regardless of what Stage 1 reported

inputs.name: near_lat_tolerance_deg
inputs.description: A taxon must have at least near_occurrence_min_n of its Stage-2-filtered records within this many degrees of latitude of lat, a cheap climate-tolerance proxy that catches a real invader whose bulk range sits many latitude degrees away from one isolated nearby record

inputs.name: near_occurrence_min_n
inputs.description: How many Stage-2-filtered records must fall within near_lat_tolerance_deg (an absolute count, not a fraction). A taxon with fewer total filtered records than this gets a proportional fallback (ALL of its few records must fall within tolerance) instead of an impossible bar

inputs.name: max_coord_uncertainty
inputs.description: Forwarded to TaxaFetch::filter_gbif_quality() (metres)

inputs.name: year_range
inputs.description: Forwarded to TaxaFetch::get_gbif_occurrences()'s Stage 2 fetch. Real default is a 2000-to-current-year window (same window every other GBIF fetcher in this ecosystem defaults to). PASS THE STUDY'S OWN WINDOW (the same year_range the main occurrence fetch used) -- every production workflow does this rather than relying on the default, so that regional evidence and resident priors are judged on the same record set. A too-wide window can let an old, geographically-distant preserved specimen inflate a species' prior (a 1929 captive-specimen record once turned an 82%-identity family-level call into a species call). Pass NULL to restore the all-time fetch

inputs.name: cache_dir
inputs.description: Forwarded to the Stage 2 fetch for checkpointing

inputs.name: verbose
inputs.description: Print per-taxon Stage 1/Stage 2 progress

output.description: One row per taxon that cleared both stages: taxon_name, weight, p_conc, source ('regional_proximity'), plus audit columns distance_km, record_year, age_years (NA when the matched record had no usable year), tile_zoom_used. Empty (correct schema, zero rows) when nothing clears Stage 1, Stage 2's quality filter, or GBIF key resolution

functions.scaling_note: One cheap GBIF-tile check per taxon (Stage 1), then a real filtered GBIF fetch only for taxa that clear it (Stage 2)

functions.name: generate_invasive_watch_evidence
functions.description: A thin evidence generator for apply_undetected_evidence(): given a plain, user-supplied list of taxa (e.g. hand-pulled from the USGS Nonindigenous Aquatic Species database or a regional invasive-species watch list), emits a fixed-weight presence-evidence row for each list member restricted to taxa that actually have a likelihood this run.

inputs.name: invasive_taxa
inputs.description: Taxon names on the watch list

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: How strongly this list's membership should pull an unobserved taxon's prior toward the singleton-mirror ceiling. No safe universal default -- an invasion risk you're highly confident about locally warrants a different weight than a precautionary watch-list entry

inputs.name: p_conc
inputs.description: How much weight the presence claim carries against future evidence (the confirmation update), in pseudo-observations. Does NOT affect the static prior's mean or concentration

inputs.name: match_list_taxa
inputs.description: Optional taxa that actually have a likelihood this run (e.g. unique(match_obj$taxon_name)). When supplied, invasive_taxa is restricted to the intersection

output.description: One row per taxon in scope: taxon_name, weight, p_conc, source ('invasive_watch'). Empty (correct schema, zero rows) when nothing is in scope

functions.scaling_note: Fast; pure R computation, no network calls

functions.name: generate_inat_range_evidence
functions.description: The third evidence generator for apply_undetected_evidence(): emits a presence-evidence row for each species whose iNaturalist geomodel range polygon covers the study site AND has sufficient observation coverage to trust that polygon, with a name-match guard against iNat's fuzzy text search silently resolving a query to a different species.

inputs.name: inat_range
inputs.description: Output of TaxaFetch::check_inat_range()

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: P(locally present) for an in-range, well-observed, name-verified species

inputs.name: p_conc
inputs.description: Presence-claim confidence in pseudo-observations (drives the confirmation update, not the static prior)

inputs.name: n_obs_threshold
inputs.description: Minimum n_observations for the range polygon to count as well-observed, matching TaxaAssign::adjust_inat_range_priors()'s established value

inputs.name: require_name_match
inputs.description: Exclude rows whose resolved iNat name differs from the query (or cannot be verified). Set FALSE only with a reviewed name mapping in hand

output.description: Evidence data frame: taxon_name, weight, p_conc, source ('inat_range'). Zero rows when nothing qualifies

functions.scaling_note: Fast; pure R computation over an already-fetched inat_range table, no new network calls

functions.name: generate_presence_curve_evidence
functions.description: Prices unobserved candidates on a shared presence-distance curve: weight = w_scale * exp(-min(distance, d_cap)/(k * d_half)). The generic version of generate_regional_proximity_evidence()'s distance-decay logic, for a caller who already has distances in hand rather than needing the two-stage GBIF-tile-then-fetch pipeline.

inputs.name: taxon_names
inputs.description: Candidate species names

inputs.name: w_scale
inputs.description: The curve's ceiling: presence probability for a species with a record at the site itself. No safe default -- calibrate against a local checklist (the GreatLakes value is 0.05)

inputs.name: distance_km
inputs.description: Distances (km), either named by taxon or positionally aligned with taxon_names. Missing/NA entries -- and the NULL default -- price at d_cap (the clamp)

inputs.name: d_half
inputs.description: The curve's e-folding half-distance in km, matching generate_regional_proximity_evidence()'s own default

inputs.name: d_cap
inputs.description: The instrument-cap distance in km beyond which the curve is flat, matching the regional generator's own fetch-buffer cap

inputs.name: k
inputs.description: Bandwidth stretch (>= 1) for listed invaders, e.g. a log-space halfway lift at their own nearest-record distance; 1 = no lift

inputs.name: p_conc
inputs.description: Passed through to apply_undetected_evidence()

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Stamped on the output rows -- 'distance_clamp' when no distances are supplied, 'presence_curve' otherwise

output.description: taxon_name, weight, p_conc, source, distance_km, k -- ready for apply_undetected_evidence()

functions.name: generate_user_specified_evidence
functions.description: The explicit policy knob from the unobserved-taxa redesign: a user may assert a presence probability for particular species of special concern (raising a watch species' chance of RESOLVING in consensus; detection itself is unaffected -- the evidence only competes for posterior mass once a candidate has a real likelihood).

inputs.name: taxon_weights
inputs.description: Names are species, values are presence probabilities in (0,1]

inputs.name: p_conc
inputs.description: Presence-claim confidence in pseudo-observations

output.description: taxon_name, weight, p_conc, source -- ready for apply_undetected_evidence()

functions.name: fit_regional_presence_curve
functions.description: The per-dataset, self-calibrating alternative to accepting generate_regional_proximity_evidence()'s default w_scale/d_half: fits a distance-to-presence curve (log-link binomial GLM) from a real presence/distance sample, e.g. a leave-the-bbox-out checklist or occurrence recipe. A zero-positive sample returns Jeffreys bounds instead of an unfittable GLM.

inputs.name: presence_df
inputs.description: Data frame with columns present (logical) and distance_km (numeric > 0): one row per species in the chosen recipe's population

inputs.name: bins
inputs.description: Distance-bin edges for the zero-positive bound table (and a fit-vs-binned diagnostic otherwise)

output.description: w_scale, d_half (fitted parameters, NA when unidentifiable); fit (the glm object or NULL); identifiable (FALSE when zero positives or a degenerate fit); bin_table (per-bin n/positives/Jeffreys 95% upper bound on P(present), plus a pooled row); n, n_present

functions.scaling_note: Fast; a single GLM fit over the presence_df sample

functions.name: report_priors
functions.description: Generate a Report Section for Prior Estimation

inputs.name: priors_output
inputs.description: Either: A list with a $priors element (contains $priors, $model, $occurrences, $grid_result) -- the shape produced by the archived build_priors() (GLMM chain, archived 2026-09-09, see archive_glmm_prior_pipeline/). Still accepted here so an OLD, already-computed build_priors() result cached on disk

inputs.name: verbose
inputs.description: Logical. Print summary messages. Default FALSE.
